title: Do LLM Decoders Listen Fairly? Benchmarking How Language Model Priors Shape Bias in Speech Recognition

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) and Max/Min Ratio (MMR) across 7 self-reported ethnicity groups (e.g., Black/African-American, White, Asian, Hispanic) using the Fair-Speech dataset.
Comparing Word Error Rate (WER), Max/Min Ratio (MMR), and hallucination/insertion rates across 6 English accent groups (e.g., Indian, African, US, England) using the Common Voice 24 dataset.
Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) and Max/Min Ratio (MMR) between male and female speakers on the Fair-Speech and Common Voice 24 datasets.
Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) and Max/Min Ratio (MMR) across multiple age brackets (e.g., Teens to 46-65) on the Fair-Speech and Common Voice 24 datasets.
Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) and Max/Min Ratio (MMR) across three self-reported socioeconomic status levels (Low, Medium, Affluent) on the Fair-Speech dataset.
Comparing Word Error Rate (WER) and Max/Min Ratio (MMR) across speakers with 21 different first languages (L1) on the Fair-Speech dataset.
